_comment: E50 (Entry 163): reviewed musical repairs, each relating the old file of a row (an identity E50a's former_identities.json recorded: a dated file a catalogue able to store a learner's material served) to the repaired file, for learner continuity only (contact, familiarity, project and encounter lookup; the reviewer's conditional approval, docs/review/responses/questions-bd7d303e.md section 4). convert.former_identities re-proves each on every build by rebuilding the old file's bytes from the repaired one (the restore lines put back, then the date, zipped under the old machine's creating system) and the build records the proved ones in provenance.formerIdentities beside E50a's. Never an approval, a parentSha256, a pdmx.json field or D2's exact-byte identity. Generated by docs/prompts/runs/E50/scripts-repaired-identities.py, never edited by hand. E50b (Entry 181; the reviewer's required change, docs/review/responses/68e0479b.md): every relation says tempoChanged, the repair changed the tempo a run of the old file was measured against, so the build also records the old identity as provenance.tempoRepairedFrom and no tempo-dependent standard reads such a run's percentage against the repaired tempo; and cuts holds the one derived repair relationship the build produced, the approved Wabash cut re-cut from its repaired parent (never a rule for other descendants), re-proved on every build by excerpts.former_cut_identities: the new cut with the parent repair's restore lines put back, zipped under the old machine's creating system, is the old cut's bytes. Learner continuity only, as above: the approval stays stale and its parentSha256 unchanged. Written by docs/prompts/runs/E50b/scripts-repaired-cut.py after E50's generator, which rewrites the file whole: a rerun of that generator is followed by this one.
